messages:
annie (support): customer on Dedicated Gold (tenant t-523) is seeing 429 throttles starting 2024-04-20T07:12Z. They claim reserved capacity, low QPS. Ticket #C-9934. 

annie (support): sample req id: req_0a1b2c3d, response had X-RateLimit: 429 and body: {"error":"throttled"}. They attached headers, says pool selected was 'shared-standard-3' not the dedicated pool.

jordan (eng-oncall): pinging @maria and @ryan. can you grab the control plane route decision for tenant t-523 around 07:12? sounds like misroute to shared pool.

escalation-bot: eskalation created to eng-platform at 07:23 UTC. priority: high.

maria (platform): on it. do we have the original request headers? annie, can you paste header snapshot (x-redwood-attrs / tier labels) they sent?

annie (support): pasted below from customer (redacted tenant id):

```
x-redwood-tenant: t-523
x-redwood-attrs: tier=gold;tenant_hash=0x7f1a;region=us-west-2
x-forwarded-for: 203.0.113.45
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
```

annie (support): they also ran a curl to reproduce:

```
curl -v -H "x-redwood-tenant: t-523" -H "x-redwood-attrs: tier=gold;tenant_hash=0x7f1a" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

annie (support): response headers from our gateway they captured:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-selected-pool: shared-standard-3
x-route-reason: tierhash-mismatch
x-debug-routing: tier_hash=0x7f1a -> bucket=42 -> pool=shared-standard-3
```

jordan (eng-oncall): interesting: x-route-reason says tierhash-mismatch. I recall a recent partial rollout of the "tierlabel normalization" change last week. could be a hash namespace shift. ryan, did we change hash salt or tier labeling in control plane?

ryan (infra): we did deploy normalization that collapses tier aliases ("gold", "premium") into canonical "gold" and also added a migration that toggles tenant mask bit ordering (feature flag net-tierhash-v2). The feature was toggled for 30% of control-plane nodes at 03:00 UTC. Possible rollout bleed.

maria (platform): if the control plane node that served this request had net-tierhash-v2 enabled, it would compute a different bucket for tenant_hash vs nodes without the flag. That would map to a different route table where tenant didn't have a dedicated pool binding -> fallback to shared. explains why dedicated pool shows low load while customer sees throttles.

jordan (eng-oncall): can we confirm by checking the control-plane decision log (route decisions) for req_0a1b2c3d? Need the node id. annie, any trace id? the customer sent x-request-id above.

annie (support): yes that's the trace id. I pulled the trace from our gateway logs:

```
2024-04-20T07:12:16Z gateway[gw-11]: req=req_0a1b2c3d -> cp-node=cp-7 -> route_decision_id=rd-88421
2024-04-20T07:12:16Z controlplane[cp-7]: evaluated policies: tier=gold, tenant_hash=0x7f1a, net-tierhash-v2=enabled -> bucket=42 -> selected_pool=shared-standard-3
```

ryan (infra): cp-7 is in the 30% rollout group. that matches. cp-7 computed bucket differently.

maria (platform): root cause likely: tierhash normalization rollout created inconsistent bucket mapping across control plane nodes. when a node with v2 talks to the routing cache that still has bindings keyed by v1 buckets, you get fallback. that triggers unintended throttling for tenants with dedicated bindings.

jordan (eng-oncall): mitigation options:
- roll back net-tierhash-v2 immediately on control plane (fast but disruptive)
- force sticky routing for affected tenant t-523 to dedicated pool via tenant override API (hotfix)
- patch routing cache to accept both v1/v2 bucket aliases (longer)

maria (platform): I can do tenant override now for t-523 to unblock. applying pin:

```
POST /controlplane/admin/tenants/t-523/override
{ "force_pool": "dedicated-gold-tenant-523", "reason": "hotfix: routing hash mismatch rollout" }
```

maria (platform): applied override at 07:34 UTC. customer confirmed 429s stopped at ~07:36.

annie (support): customer reports normal behavior now, thanks. they're still worried about other tenants. any idea scope?

ryan (infra): scanning route decisions across cp-7..cp-12 in rollout slice for last 6 hours: found ~12 tenants with similar fallback decisions (non-zero). only 3 reported by customers so far. seems limited but real.

jordan (eng-oncall): next steps:
- rollback net-tierhash-v2 on control plane rollout (ryan) OR pause rollout while we deploy compatibility mapping.
- backfill routing cache to include alias buckets for v1/v2 for 24h (maria/infra).
- notify customers for any tenants affected and run audit of tenant overrides to remove after fix.
- postmortem and update rollout playbook to require canary traffic validation for tiered routing.

maria (platform): I'll schedule immediate rollback for the rollout group and open a follow-up change to add aliasing in the cache. putting change request in change queue now.

ryan (infra): rolling back cp nodes in slice starting 07:50 UTC. I'll post progress.

escalation-bot: rollback job started for cp nodes [cp-5..cp-10] at 07:51 UTC.

jordan (eng-oncall): thanks team. annie, please keep customer updated and include timeline for root cause + follow-up. I'll own the postmortem doc.

annie (support): will do. customer is appreciative of the quick hotfix. I'll attach the tenant override details and the rollback confirmation. :white_check_mark:
